narration.headline: different properties: correlation -0.0172 across 25 cells; no other statistic between them is returned
narration.framing: model-vs-model agreement (no ground truth), not accuracy

result.method: pointwise pixel-value sampled on a grid over the shared extent (an estimate, not every pixel); windows where either map is no-data are dropped before any statistic; no ground truth, so this is model-vs-model agreement (no ground truth), not accuracy.
result.warning: the results measure different properties (['sample_karst_score', 'sample_number']), so their values are different quantities: only the correlation (whether they rise and fall together) is meaningful, and it is the only statistic returned between them. A mean difference, an RMSE, an agreement fraction or an ensemble spread would mix two quantities, so none is computed; do not work one out, and do not say one reads higher than the other.
result.sampling_note: the 6x6 grid has 36 cells; each of the 2 results was sampled once per cell, so 72 samples were requested; 25 compared, 11 dropped (no-data or failed in either map; n_nodata_dropped and n_failed_dropped count those cells)
result.nodata_rule: a sample is no-data, and never enters a statistic, when its band is missing or NaN, equals the model's nodata_value, lies outside the band's declared regression range, or carries no class on a classification band

draft:
Compared both completed 2025 predictions on the PA Karst project. Key finding: they measure **different quantities**, so a direct "where they differ" map doesn't exist.

| Item | KarstBinary | KarstNumber |
|---|---|---|
| Result id | `419c581d…f26b` | `afb1cf68…9ae8` |
| Property | `sample_karst_score` (0.0–1.0) | `sample_number` (0.2–1.2) |
| Model type | fine_tuned, per-pixel regression | fine_tuned, per-pixel regression |
| Mean over shared grid | 0.10049 | 0.681763 |

**How they relate:** sampled on a 6x6 grid over the shared extent (~10,091 km²); 25 cells compared, 11 dropped as no-data in either map. Correlation between the two bands: **-0.0172** — essentially zero, i.e. they do not rise and fall together. Because the bands are different quantities, no difference/RMSE/agreement statistics are meaningful, and the tool correctly refused them.

**Which is right:** neither can be declared right from this comparison alone — there is no ground-truth label set here, so model-vs-model agreement is not accuracy, and since the outputs aren't even the same quantity, the low correlation doesn't establish that either is wrong. It does suggest they are capturing different signals (a binary-style karst score vs. a count-like number).

If you want a verdict, the next step is to label a small window set from each map and I'll compute an error rate per map with `olmoearth_plan_label_sample` + `olmoearth_estimate_map_error`. Tell me how many windows you can review (e.g. 20–30) and I'll generate the labeled review sets.
